Question: Are edibles fast acting?
Answer: No, edibles are actually one of the slowest-acting ways to ingest cannabis. The activation tine varies considerably, but the gummies I take usually don't kick in until around 45 minutes to an hour which is pretty typical for edibles. You'll start to feel higher doses sooner than smaller ones. It'll kick in faster on an empty stomach and slower if you just ate a meal when you ingest. Edibles keep you high much longer, too. I'll typically start sobering up from a joint after an hour or two, but a 25 mg THC edible will keep me high for 10 or more hours. Keep in mind I'm a large dude (235 lbs), so smaller people will be even more strongly affected. My sister-in-law who weighs 100 lbs less than me once had an edible brownie with about a 30 mg THC dose and was high for almost a full 24 hours. If you want to have an edible you have to plan your day around it.

Question: Why is there no Christians, Muslims and Judaism in Star Trek? Is it because it's the natural progression of the human race?
Answer: There are, they just don't openly proselytize. I'm assuming the question asker is from the USA, which is an overtly religious society, especially among Evangelical and Fundamentalist Christians, and religious issues are just part of the public discourse. That is actually a rarity among societies, and most places in the world treat religion as a private function. Human religions in the Star Trek Canon seem to have universally adopted this system. It's no secret that Gene Roddenberry was an atheist and insisted that there were no human religions being practiced but this was contradicted as early as the 1st season of the Original Series. The episode “Balance of Terror” began with Kirk officiating a wedding in the Enterprise's chapel. In the episode “Who Mourns For Adonais?” Kirk tells the being claiming to be the god Apollo “Mankind has no need for Gods. We find the one quite adequate,” implying that Kirk holds some type of monotheistic belief. In Star Trek II, during Spock's funeral, Scotty plays the Christian hymn “Amazing Grace” on the bagpipe. In the TNG episode “Sub Rosa,” a priest performs an Anglican funeral rite for Beverly Crusher's deceased grandmother. On Deep Space 9, while Ben Sisko and Cassidy Yates were planning their wedding, Cassidy mentioned that her mother would want her to be married by a minister. On Enterprise Dr Phlox mentioned that he once attended a Roman Catholic mass in St Peter's Square in the Vatican. Islam and Judaism are not mentioned much in Star Trek, although in an early script for the TNG episode “Family” Worf's adoptive parents were explicitly mentioned to be Jewish. Other human religions are mentioned or shown however, for instance Chakotay's Native American religious practices. Dr Phlox also studied Buddhism and Hinduism while visiting Earth. So human religions are still practiced in the Star Trek universe.
